stem: For what value of $a$ does the equation $5(ax - 2) + 3x = 13(x + 1) - 7$ have no solution?
explanation: Expanding both sides: the left side becomes $5ax - 10 + 3x = (5a + 3)x - 10$, and the right side becomes $13x + 13 - 7 = 13x + 6$. Rearranging gives $(5a + 3 - 13)x = 16$, which simplifies to $(5a - 10)x = 16$. For the equation to have no solution, the coefficient of $x$ must be zero while the constant is nonzero. Setting $5a - 10 = 0$ gives $a = 2$. Since $16 \neq 0$, the equation has no solution when $a = 2$.
